title: Retry safety horizon and idempotency conventions for multi-lang SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Different Redwood language SDKs (Python/TS/Go) have diverging retry defaults, idempotency token formats, and streaming resume semantics. Customers (platform and product teams) see inconsistent behaviour across runtimes: duplicate operations, unclear client responsibilities, and insufficient telemetry to debug retry-induced anomalies. We need a cross-SDK specification that balances safety (avoid duplicates), developer ergonomics, and debuggability for both unary and streaming APIs.
proposal: Introduce a unified 'retry safety horizon' concept: a configurable deduplication window (default 60s) that clients use when generating idempotency tokens and when deciding resends. Standardize token format, rotation, and lifecycle. Define a clear error taxonomy mapped to retryability for the SDKs and provide language-specific helper primitives (generators, middleware) and observability labels. Provide safe streaming resume hooks that combine resume cursors and optional idempotency tokens scoped by conversation/request. Ship as opt-in in 2025 Q1, then enable as default after field validation.
design_notes:
- Token format: prefix version (v1), sdk shorthand, unix epoch seconds, random 128-bit suffix (base64url) e.g. v1-py-1700000000-<b64>. This allows quick heuristics in logs and server-side retention TTLs.
- Safety horizon default: 60s for user-triggered mutate-like operations; 10s for single-shot generation calls by default unless caller marks high-cost idempotent=true.
- Server expectations: Servers accept tokens and store short-lived dedup keys; server-side dedup is best-effort. Clients must not rely exclusively on server dedup for correctness.
- Streaming: For resumable streams, provide two orthogonal primitives: resume_cursor (server-sent) and resume_hint_token (client-generated idempotency token tied to logical request). Resume flow: client reconnects with resume_cursor if available; if not, SDK may reissue request using same resume_hint_token within safety horizon to avoid duplicate side-effects.
- Observability: SDKs emit retry_attempt, retry_reason, idempotency_token, and safety_horizon_ms as structured labels. We will standardize label names across SDKs for easy aggregation in Console.
implementation_plan:
1) API/SDK spec PR (this ticket) describing enums, defaults, and examples (Python/TS/Go).
2) Implement token utilities and middleware in each SDK: generator, header attachment, opt-in automatic retry wrapping.
3) Add streaming helpers: resume cursor handling, backoff-aware reconnect.
4) Add telemetry hooks in SDKs and Console ingestion parsers.
5) Dogfood: enable for internal infra routes and collect metrics for 2 weeks.
6) Iterate and flip default if metrics show reduced duplicates and no user friction.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-SDK spec merged in docs repo and linked from SDKs
Python/TS/Go SDKs expose idempotency token generator API with identical semantics
Retry defaults documented and implemented: conservative defaults with override options
Streaming helpers available and documented with sample code in each SDK
Telemetry emitted to Console with consistent label names and dashboards updated
Dogfood run completed and metrics (duplicate rate, user errors) evaluated

notes: Key trade-offs discussed with API and Runtime: longer safety horizon reduces duplicates but increases state retention cost on server. We default conservative horizon and provide explicit opt-in for longer windows for batched/billing-sensitive workflows. For function/tool-calls, recommend idempotency=true for side-effects and SDKs will expose a flag to suppress automatic retry when true.
examples: Python token generator: token = IdempotencyToken.generate(sdk='py', ttl_seconds=60) --> 'v1-py-1700000000-xxxxxxxx'
TS helper: const token = idempotency.create({sdk:'ts', ttl:60}); headers['Idempotency-Token'] = token
Go usage: token := idemp.New("go", 60*time.Second); req.Header.Set("Idempotency-Token", token.String())
Streaming resume (pseudo): onDisconnect -> if (cursor) reconnect with cursor; else if (token && withinSafetyHorizon) resend with same token to avoid duplicate side-effect
